input.quote: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 commits Corio to an initial five-year term with automatic one-year renewals, and Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. No convenience exit exists for Corio anywhere in the Agreement (the exits at p0050 and p0079 are acceptance-test and warranty remedies), so the bargain fails even the fallback, which requires a Customer convenience right on 60-90 days' notice. The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so it is not flagged here. We therefore insert Section 11.4 carrying the four preferred elements: Corio (identified expressly as Commerce One's customer, since "CUSTOMER(S)" is defined in Section 1.6 as Corio's own customers) may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice, Commerce One refunds prepaid fees pro rata, and Commerce One has no convenience right during the initial or renewal terms. The section number is embedded so the survival list and cross-references remain clean, and no partial-termination language is added because there is no Order Form structure.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 11.4 giving Corio (as Commerce One's customer) convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and barring Commerce One convenience termination during the initial and renewal terms.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11 leaves us with no convenience exit across a five-year committed term, so we have added Section 11.4 allowing Corio, as Commerce One's customer, to terminate on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Commerce One has no convenience right during the initial or renewal terms. We can move to 60-90 days' notice as a fallback if needed.

ops.text: 11.4 Termination for Convenience. Corio, as Commerce One's customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
